name: Third-Country Work Permit (B/L, quota-based)

selection_odds.basis: 2026 federal quota frozen at 8,500 total (4,500 B + 4,000 L), unchanged from 2025, confirmed 19 November 2025. Additional 3,500 permits for EU/EFTA service providers (3,000 L + 500 B) and 3,500 for UK nationals (2,100 B + 1,400 L).

requirements.blocker_text: This requires the employer to prove no suitable Swiss/EU-EFTA candidate was available (priority of domestic workers / Inländervorrang), overall economic interest of Switzerland, and quota availability at the cantonal level.
requirements.fix_path: Secure a qualifying job offer from an employer prepared to complete the priority test.

requirements.blocker_text: This is generally restricted to managers, specialists, and other qualified workers — typically requiring a university degree and several years of relevant experience.

value.note: B permits; separate 4,000 L permit quota also applies

requirements.blocker_text: This is subject to the annual federal quota (4,500 B + 4,000 L for 2026), distributed to cantons, which can be exhausted before year-end in high-demand cantons.

evidence_required.document: Degree certificate and evidence of relevant professional experience

Federal Council quota decision for 2026, 19 November 2025

notes: FORMULA VALUE, tier-1 confirmed and genuinely frozen year-over-year: 8,500 total quota (4,500 B + 4,000 L) unchanged from 2025. Confirmed utilization context: as of end-2024, companies had used 74% of the available quota, well below full exhaustion — worth flagging since demand doesn't always match the headline cap. Duration (1 year, third-country) is genuinely shorter than the EU/EFTA equivalent's 5-year B permit — the same underlying permit letter (B) means something structurally different depending on which of Switzerland's two tiers the holder falls into, a real and confirmed asymmetry central to the whole Swiss system. No national minimum wage exists (Switzerland has none federally; a handful of cantons set their own) — so unlike most other countries' work-sponsored routes in this dataset, there's no single salary-threshold figure to encode; the market-rate test is comparative rather than absolute.
